source_kind: offline postprocessing of existing complete candidate trace
method: Strict original prepare used only to obtain fixed model. Reset and step APIs blocked. Each recorded qpos/qvel/ctrl/time copied to independent MjData; mj_forward and mj_subtreeVel there only. No recomputed force used as applied-force evidence.
geometry_scope: Recomputed instantaneous ground-contact geometry; hull is convex hull of penetrating foot contact points, not a hardware support polygon. Signed margin positive inside. Foot origins and body forward axes are model frames. Capture-point proxy COM+v_xy*sqrt(COM_z/g) assumes fixed-height point-mass dynamics and is a qualitative instability diagnostic, not an independent success criterion.
time_semantics: Recorded synchronized standing measurements and snapshot positions are post-step. Recorded integration torque/load uses the interval beginning at integration_pre_elapsed_s.
fixed_fore_aft_basis_definition: Horizontal mean foot-body +X axis at recorded t=3.75 s, held fixed for subsequent projections; posterior is the negative direction. This is a model-frame direction, not a recovered support polygon.
facts: No stable-standing window occurred. Maximum pelvis height 0.5809608409731037m remained below 0.6052459924998083m; minimum torso tilt after 3s was 24.392468545210438deg, above 15deg.
Both feet carry load again around 4.0-4.75s, but recorded COM speed increases before support loss and the torso subsequently falls posteriorly.
Instantaneous foot geometry usually has fewer than three distinct penetrating contact points; polygon margins are null rather than fabricated.
inferences: The slower reference arrests the original strong launch but does not complete the rise or arrest posterior COM drift. Later torso impact is a consequence of the failed balance transition rather than evidence of a large initial landing impulse.
Late knee extension and forward body-over-feet placement must be coordinated; preserving old joint endpoints alone does not preserve the old global stance or momentum.
